summary: Build a produce-focused visit around Muang Mai’s working wholesale market and, if your dates include Saturday or Sunday, Jing Jai Farmers Market. December brings the start of Chiang Mai strawberry harvest, with locally grown citrus and other cool-season fruit also worth asking about; actual stalls and harvest quality vary by week.
whyGo: Compare a busy everyday wholesale market with Jing Jai’s weekend farmer stalls, where the operator says Chiang Mai-area growers sell fruit, vegetables and organic or chemical-free produce.
Look for early-season Chiang Mai strawberries and ask vendors what is local and currently at peak, rather than assuming every northern fruit is in season.
bestFor: Food-curious travelers who enjoy browsing, tasting and buying produce directly from market vendors.
Visitors with a Saturday or Sunday morning free for Jing Jai, or an early weekday start for Muang Mai.
skipIf: You expect a curated farm tour, guaranteed organic certification at every stall, or fixed fruit varieties and prices.
You need confirmed step-free routes, quiet aisles or detailed accessibility facilities.
duration: Allow 45–90 minutes at one market, or about 2–3 hours to visit both including the transfer. These are planning estimates; Muang Mai is a spread-out working market and Jing Jai is best visited during its morning market hours.
cost: No admission is listed for either market. Set a flexible shopping budget: prices vary by fruit, grade, quantity and vendor, and no dependable December 2026 price list was found. Ask the price and unit before purchase; carry small Thai baht notes.
hours: Jing Jai’s official site lists Jing Jai Farmers Market on Saturday and Sunday, 06:30–15:00; the broader Jing Jai Market site opens later on weekdays. Muang Mai is a daily working market, but stall hours vary and no official current schedule was found; early morning is the practical target. Check venue updates near the visit, especially for year-end holidays.
bestTime: For Jing Jai, arrive around 07:00–09:00 on Saturday or Sunday for the morning farmers market and widest browsing time. For Muang Mai, aim for roughly 06:00–08:00 to see active produce trade. Go early in December for seasonal interest: Chiang Mai Agriculture Office’s 2025/26 strawberry outlook gives harvest as October–April, with the largest volume expected in January, so December is early season rather than the peak.
gettingThere: Muang Mai sits north of Warorot in the Ping River market district; from the Old City use a songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail, or walk over from Warorot. Jing Jai Market is at 45 Atsadathon Road; ride-hail or songthaew is practical from the Old City. Travel time and fares depend on pickup point and traffic; allow a buffer during the year-end period.
booking: No ticket or booking is indicated for market browsing. Go independently; for a specific product, ask a vendor shortly before visiting because harvest and stock change. Confirm price, quantity and whether a sample is offered before buying.
accessibility: No reliable step-free or accessibility information was found. Muang Mai is a working market with wet or uneven floors, carts and vehicle movements; Jing Jai is a busy outdoor market. Ask the venue directly about access needs before relying on either for a wheelchair or mobility-limited visit.
practicalTips: At Jing Jai, ask whether strawberries are from Chiang Mai province and when they were picked; the official provincial outlook predicts a season, not stock at a particular stall.
Expect prices to vary by variety, quality and pack size. Compare a couple of stalls and confirm the price per kilogram or box before paying; no verified current price benchmark is available.
At Muang Mai, keep out of loading lanes and give vendors room to weigh and move produce. Ask before photographing people or close-ups of their stalls.
For ready-to-eat fruit, choose freshly cut portions kept covered or chilled where possible; wash whole fruit with safe water before eating and peel it yourself if unsure about washing water.
Wear shoes with grip, bring small cash and a reusable bag, and keep purchases cool if you plan to carry berries for long.
decemberNotes: For December 2026, prioritize strawberries as a plausible early-season Chiang Mai crop, with supply likely to build toward the provincial January peak reported for 2025/26. The provincial office also tracks Sai Nam Phueng oranges, persimmons and other fruit, but market stock and timing can shift by weather and farm. Jing Jai Farmers Market runs on weekends; Muang Mai suits a weekday or early start. Christmas and New Year market schedules are not published this far ahead, so check the official Jing Jai page and current local listings close to the date.
uncertainties: The Chiang Mai strawberry forecast is for the 2025/26 crop year; it supports the usual seasonal window but cannot guarantee 2026/27 harvest timing, quality or December stall availability.
Muang Mai lacks a reliable official schedule and published prices; vendor hours, wholesale activity and retail stock vary.
Jing Jai’s official weekend farmers market hours are published, but its year-end 2026 holiday adjustments and accessibility details are not confirmed.
